My philosophy 

I envision the process of learning a language as the process of growing a tree: it will need patience and care, we can not make instant results, the best we can do is use a fertilizer which in my case is a group of technics and in the end enjoy the sweet fruit of success!

teacher_info.about_teacher: The way I see language learning is a bit philosophical but it also came from my personal experience after being both a student and a teacher for a while. I envision the process of language learning to be similar to the process of growing a tree; you need patience and take care of the plant on a regular basis to get a result that normally can not be pushed ahead of time...But you can always add-in some fertilizers (which are in my case a certain set of technics) to get improved results in terms of time and quality.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
Lessons: I prefer that you book packages to show commitment and also to get along with the nature of the process ( as I explained earlier: expect to practice on a regular basis ! ), I am very flexible and I don't have a problem canceling or reporting lessons... I can also use instant messaging apps like Whatsapp if you feel like learning and practicing on the go. 
Let's talk technics: I am not a big fan of the Pimsleur method unless it's used with some other tools to remember the vocabulary you learned. For example, Anki flashcards. I prefer to rely on the spaced repetition system proposed by apps like Duolingo and Memrise.

pro_course_detail.title: Arabic (Maghrebi) for communication
pro_course_detail.description:
I'll teach you letters of the Arabic alphabet and written texts are read from right to left, and you'll learn Arabic quickly by focusing on basic daily words that could help with conversation and understanding.

Familiarize yourself with some basic Arabic words like "marhaban" for hello, "ma'a ssalamah" for goodbye, "aahlan wa sahlan bika" for welcome, "kabeer" for big, "sagheer" for small, "Alyawm" for today, "akala" for eating, or "dahaba" to go.

We will focus on: 
 - Read texts in Arabic: The best way to learn Arabic is to read in the original language. The more you read in the new language, the more your brain will get accustomed to the sounds and turns of phrases. 
 - Listening to the Arabic language: It's important to immerse yourself in Arab culture and to hear Arabic native speakers in order to learn the language and boost your beginner level. 
 - Regularly learn vocabulary: to improve your written and oral comprehension, I will assist you to translate words from English-Arabic or French-Arabic. The more vocabulary you learn, the more you will be able to master the language.

pro_course_detail.title: English for beginners (Grammar, reading, spelling)
pro_course_detail.description:

Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing are the main skills you need to communicate in any language. Being very good at only one of these skills will not help you to communicate. I’ll assist you to acquire these 4 skills. You will be able to listen and speak correctly with good pronunciation. It helps for your daily conversations.
To acquire these skills, we will use for: 
-	Listening: Use Internet listening resources or recording to familiarize you with the language.
-	Speaking: we can have conversations about different topics to practice pronunciation.
-	Reading: we can use children's books, simplified readers (Penguin), newspapers, magazines, Internet sites, novels, and much more...
-	Writing: Don't always pay attention to grammar. Free writing can be very useful. It can show you that writing is fun. Have fun with the language.
